title: HLS playlist renderer with latency histogram
name: Playlist rendering service

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles its hot path (rendering, caching and timing playlist requests)? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two threads call get(100) at the same moment on a cold cache. What happens?
choices: The second thread blocks until the first finishes rendering, so the playlist is built once.
Both may render the playlist, but only the first inserted entry is kept and both callers get a valid pointer to cached content.
The shared_mutex deadlocks because a shared lock is held while a unique lock is requested.
The second thread's insertion overwrites the first, invalidating the pointer the first caller holds.

questions.prompt: After the cache reaches max_entries_ and is cleared, what happens to a playlist string a request thread obtained earlier and is still writing to a socket?
choices: It becomes a dangling reference and the thread must copy it first.
It is freed immediately by clear(), so the write fails.
It remains valid, because the shared_ptr keeps the string alive until the last holder releases it.
It is moved into the new cache generation.
